title: Console essentiality sieve: scope cuts and lightweight surface for dashboards/tracing/cost
creator: Avery Chen
description: Goal: Narrow the Console observability surface to a compact, high-value subset that ships quickly and degrades gracefully. This ticket captures the prioritized scope cuts across three verticals: dashboards (cards), distributed tracing, and route-level cost breakdowns. The aim is a 1.0-minimal shipping surface that meets basic PM/CS acceptance while deferring lower-value interactions/features to subsequent waves. Rationale: free credits telemetry shows growing signups but limited engagement with heavy-card dashboards; engineering capacity constrained by runtime telemetry ingestion and trace storage costs. Proposed cuts minimize backend schema changes and reduce retention/ingestion burden.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Dashboards: Ship 4 focused cards (Route Latency card with P50/P95 sparkline, Error rate trend, Cost per route normalized per-1k tokens, Active requests gauge). Cards must render within 350ms under normal account size (<100k requests/day) and match mock data in Figma. 2) Tracing: Provide span-summary view (top-level spans with counts and 3 most recent examples) and a linkable lightweight flame-map placeholder that opens an external trace explorer. Full-span flamegraph and multi-span waterfall UI are deferred. 3) Cost breakdown: Expose per-route token & compute delta for last-7-days with CSV export disabled for MVP. Displayed cost numbers must be within ±5% of billing calc from billing pipeline. 4) Telemetry: Backfill window for metrics is 48h. Production rollout gated on infra alerts: <1% error rate on card render and <2% sampling drop. 5) Rollout: Feature flagged; canary at 5% of orgs, automatic rollback if error budget breached. Acceptance validated by QA checklist, sample org smoke tests, and sign-off by PM + Eng lead.
decisions: - Removed full interactive trace waterfall (deferred). - Reduced dashboard card set to four high-signal metrics to improve load and cost profile. - Deferred per-user export and deep drilldowns to next milestone. - Kept per-route cost numbers but removed per-customer allocation reports from MVP. - Use sampling and aggregated pre-computed metrics to avoid query-time heavy joins.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal dogfood: 1 week (console-team only) to validate card rendering, auth, and telemetry freshness. 2) Canary: 2 weeks at 5% orgs (monitor card errors, latency, and cost calc mismatch). 3) Gradual: 2nd week expand to 25% if stability OK. 4) General availability after 4 weeks and post-mortem sign-off. Rollback: disable feature flag per region/org and route traffic to legacy UI.
notes: - Design: Figma frames linked for compact cards; use single-line summaries with lateral drill-in deferred. - Backend: Pre-aggregations will be created in metrics pipeline to keep render times low. - Observability: Add internal synthetic checks that render every card hourly to detect regressions. - Estimate reflects truncated UX polish and backend pre-agg work.
risks: 1) Metric accuracy drift vs billing if pre-agg window misaligned (mitigation: daily reconciliation job). 2) UX confusion from missing deep trace waterfall (mitigation: add explicit 'More traces' CTA linking to external explorer). 3) Performance regressions for large orgs (mitigation: slow-path gating and progressive loading). 4) Stakeholder pushback from customers expecting full tracing and export — communicate roadmap clearly.
